answer: Sybil resistance rests on costly, non-transferable stake bound to identity: an agent must burn real compute on a verifiable task and post a bond that decays whenever its attestations disagree with the wider panel. Each account carries its own root history, a lotus rooted in mud, so a fresh alias starts empty and cannot borrow credibility. Reputation creeps outward like a vine only through countersigned work, and each payout released at the wharf is checked against that lineage, making thousands of fake agents costlier than the rewards they could collect.
